orbits-s2.title: A satellite in a circular orbit
orbits-s2.html: A 200 kg satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 4.0 × 10⁶ m (measured from the planet’s center) around a planet of mass 6.4 × 10²³ kg. G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². Take UG = 0 at infinite separation. The satellite’s mass is much smaller than the planet’s.

items.q: What is the rotational inertia of the turntable and clay together about the axle?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the disk alone. Add the clay as a point object, mr².
Value: that uses MR² for the disk. A solid disk has I = ½MR² (given).

items.q: What is the rotational kinetic energy of the turntable and clay? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: ω was not squared. K = ½Iω².
Value: the ½ is missing. K = ½Iω².

items.q: The turntable’s center does not move. Which statement about its kinetic energy is correct?
options: It has kinetic energy, because every piece of it is moving
It has no kinetic energy, because its center of mass is at rest
It has no kinetic energy, because opposite sides cancel out
Its kinetic energy is at the rim, where the speed is largest

items.q: The turntable is sped up to 12 rad/s. Its rotational kinetic energy becomes
options: 4 times as large
2 times as large
the same
8 times as large

items.q: What share of the total rotational kinetic energy belongs to the clay?
Which graph of these data gives a straight line through the origin?
options: K against ω²
K against ω
K against 1/ω
√K against ω²

items.q: Use the data to find the flywheel’s rotational inertia.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the slope of K against ω², which is ½I. Double it.
Value: that divides by ω instead of ω². K = ½Iω², so I = 2K/ω².

items.q: Predict the flywheel’s kinetic energy at 50 rad/s.
An engineer wants a flywheel of the same mass and radius to store more energy at the same ω. She should
options: move more of its mass to the rim
move more of its mass toward the axle
make it a solid disk instead of a ring
leave the shape, since K depends on mass

items.q: Rotational kinetic energy is
options: a scalar, measured in joules
a vector along the axis, in joules
a scalar, measured in N·m/s
a vector, measured in kg·m²/s

items.q: A small flywheel with rotational inertia 0.050 kg·m² spins at 300 rad/s. How much kinetic energy does it store?

mistakes.why: Value: ω was not squared. K = ½Iω².

items.q: A wheel with rotational inertia 0.40 kg·m² has 25 J of rotational kinetic energy. How fast is it turning?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ω². Take the square root.
Value: the ½ was dropped. ω = √(2K/I).

items.q: A solid disk and a hoop of the same mass and radius spin at the same angular velocity about their centers (disk I = ½MR², hoop I = MR², given). Compared with the disk, the hoop has
options: twice the rotational kinetic energy
the same rotational kinetic energy
half the rotational kinetic energy
four times the rotational kinetic energy

items.q: A figure skater spins on frictionless ice. Ignoring her arms, she is modeled as a cylinder. Predict how each quantity changes if, at the same angular velocity, she were twice as wide (same mass, cylinder radius doubled).

variables.name: The angular velocity she would need to keep her original rotational kinetic energy

items.q: A solid cylinder of mass 0.60 kg and radius 0.15 m (I = ½MR², given) spins at 20 rad/s about its central axis. What is its rotational kinetic energy?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses MR². A solid cylinder has I = ½MR².
Value: R was not squared in I = ½MR².

items.q: Why does a spinning wheel’s rotational kinetic energy not depend on whether it turns clockwise or counterclockwise?
options: ω is squared, so its sign drops out
Kinetic energy depends on the mass and not the motion
The two directions have different rotational inertias
Clockwise turning has negative kinetic energy

items.q: What torque does the rope exert on the drum while the bucket rises at constant speed?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the force by the radius. τ = rF.
Value: that uses the mass instead of the rope’s force. At constant speed the tension is mg.

items.q: How much work does the crank do on the drum while it turns through 25.0 rad? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies the torque by the angle in revolutions (25.0 rad ÷ 2π = 3.98 rev). W = τΔθ needs the angle in radians.
Value: that converts 25.0 rad to degrees. W = τΔθ needs radians.

items.q: How far does the bucket rise?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the angle by r. The rope wound up is s = rθ.
Value: that treats 25.0 rad as 25.0 revolutions. s = rθ with θ in radians.

items.q: How does the work done by the torque on the drum compare with the increase in the bucket’s gravitational potential energy?
options: They are equal: nothing speeds up and there is no friction
The work is larger, because some goes into spinning the drum
The work is smaller, because the drum’s radius is small
The work is a rotational quantity, so it is not an energy

items.q: How much work does the motor do on the wheel from 0 to 8.0 rad?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides torque by angle. Work is the area under the τ-θ graph: τΔθ.

items.q: How much work does the motor do on the wheel from 0 to 14.0 rad?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 6.0 N·m for the whole 14.0 rad. From 8.0 to 14.0 rad the torque falls to zero: take the triangle’s area.
Value: that stops at 8.0 rad. Add the triangle from 8.0 to 14.0 rad.

items.q: The wheel (I = 0.50 kg·m²) starts from rest on a frictionless axle. How fast is it turning at 14.0 rad?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ω². Take the square root.
Value: the ½ was dropped. W = ½Iω², so ω = √(2W/I).

items.q: Between 8.0 rad and 14.0 rad, the wheel
options: keeps speeding up, more and more gently
slows down, because the torque is decreasing
turns at a constant angular velocity
speeds up more and more quickly

items.q: The work done on a wheel by a constant torque τ while it turns through an angle Δθ is
options: τΔθ, with Δθ in radians
τΔθ, with Δθ in degrees
τ/Δθ
½τΔθ²

items.q: A screwdriver applies a constant torque of 1.5 N·m while turning a screw through 4 full revolutions. How much work is done?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 4 as the angle. Convert revolutions to radians: 4 × 2π rad.
Value: that uses degrees. W = τΔθ needs radians.

items.q: A wheel turns counterclockwise. A brake exerts a clockwise torque on it. The work done by the brake’s torque is
options: negative, and the wheel loses kinetic energy
positive, because the torque is not zero
zero, because a brake does not move
negative, and the wheel gains kinetic energy

items.q: A wheel with I = 2.0 kg·m² spins at 15 rad/s. A brake stops it while the wheel turns through 30 rad. What constant braking torque does this take?

mistakes.why: Value: ω was not squared in ½Iω².
Value: the ½ in ½Iω² was dropped.

items.q: On a graph of torque against angle for a wheel, what does the area under the line represent?
options: The work done on the wheel
The wheel’s angular velocity
The wheel’s angular acceleration
The wheel’s rotational inertia

items.q: A motor applies the same constant torque to two wheels, starting from rest, through the same angle. Wheel 2 has twice the rotational inertia of wheel 1. Compared with wheel 1, wheel 2 ends with
options: the same kinetic energy and a smaller angular velocity
half the kinetic energy and the same angular velocity
the same kinetic energy and the same angular velocity
twice the kinetic energy and the same angular velocity

items.q: A constant torque spins up a wheel from rest on a frictionless axle. Predict how each quantity changes as the wheel turns through more and more angle.

variables.name: Work done on the wheel so far
The time the wheel takes to make each successive full turn

items.q: What is the size of the puck’s angular momentum about point P? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the linear momentum, mv. Multiply by the lever arm: L = mvd.
Value: d is not squared for a point object. L = r m v sin θ = mvd.

items.q: As the puck slides on past P, its distance r from P grows. Its angular momentum about P
options: stays the same, because r sin θ stays 0.40 m
grows, because r grows
shrinks, because the puck moves away from P
is zero, because the puck is not turning

items.q: What is the puck’s angular momentum about point Q, which lies on its path?
options: Zero
0.24 kg·m²/s
0.60 kg·m²/s
It depends on how far the puck is from Q

items.q: A second puck of the same mass slides at 6.0 m/s along a parallel line 0.20 m from P. Compared with the first puck, its angular momentum about P is
options: the same
twice as large
half as large
four times as large

items.q: What angular impulse does the torque deliver from 0 to 2.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides torque by time. Angular impulse is τΔt, the area under the τ-t graph.

items.q: The wheel starts at rest. What is its angular velocity at 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies L by I. ω = L/I.
Value: that uses the torque for 3.0 s. The torque is zero after 2.0 s.

items.q: What is the wheel’s angular momentum at 6.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that adds the last part of the area. From 4.0 to 6.0 s the torque is negative, so it removes angular momentum.
Value: that ignores the negative torque from 4.0 to 6.0 s.

items.q: Which describes the graph of the wheel’s angular momentum against time from 4.0 s to 6.0 s?
options: A straight line sloping down, with slope −2.0 N·m
A horizontal line, because L is conserved
A straight line sloping up, because the wheel still turns counterclockwise
A vertical drop to zero at 4.0 s

items.q: For a rigid object turning about a fixed axis, angular momentum is
options: L = Iω, in kg·m²/s
L = ½Iω², in joules
L = Iα, in N·m
L = mv, in kg·m/s

items.q: A bicycle wheel with I = 0.25 kg·m² spins at 12 rad/s. What is its angular momentum?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½Iω², the kinetic energy in joules. L = Iω.

items.q: A torque of 0.60 N·m acts on a spinning top for 0.50 s in the direction it spins. By how much does its angular momentum change?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides torque by time. ΔL = τΔt.

items.q: A ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius 0.50 m at 2.0 m/s around a post. A student says the ball has no angular momentum about the post because it is a point object, not a spinning body. Which response is correct?
options: It does: about the post, L = rmv sin 90° = rmv
It does not: a point object has no rotational inertia
It does not: its velocity keeps changing direction
It does, but just while the string is speeding it up

items.q: A graph of a wheel’s angular momentum against time is a horizontal line. What does that tell you?
options: The net torque on the wheel is zero
The wheel is not turning
The wheel’s angular acceleration is constant and nonzero
A constant torque is acting on the wheel

items.q: Two wheels have the same angular momentum. Wheel A has twice the rotational inertia of wheel B. Wheel A’s angular velocity is
options: half of wheel B’s
twice wheel B’s
the same as wheel B’s
one quarter of wheel B’s

items.q: A torque acts on a wheel for a short time. Which change in the wheel is set directly by the angular impulse τΔt?
options: Its change in angular momentum
Its change in rotational kinetic energy
Its rotational inertia
Its angular acceleration

items.q: A puck slides in a straight line at constant speed past a point P on a frictionless table. Predict how each quantity changes as the puck moves from far left of P to the point of its path closest to P.

variables.name: The puck’s distance r from P
sin θ, where θ is the angle between the puck’s velocity and the line from P to the puck
The puck’s angular momentum about P

items.q: What is the student’s angular velocity after pulling the weights in?

mistakes.why: Value: the ratio is upside down. I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂, so a smaller I gives a larger ω.
Value: that keeps kinetic energy constant. The conserved quantity is L = Iω.

items.q: Why is the angular momentum of the student, weights and stool the same before and after?
options: No net torque about the axle comes from outside the system
Angular momentum is conserved whatever acts on a system
The student pulls the weights in slowly
The student’s arms exert no force on the weights

items.q: By how much does the rotational kinetic energy of the system change?

mistakes.why: Value: kinetic energy is not conserved here. The student does work pulling the weights in.
Value: that is the final kinetic energy. Subtract the initial 6.0 J.

items.q: Where does the extra rotational kinetic energy come from?
options: Work done by her muscles pulling the weights in
The floor, through the stool’s axle
Nowhere: kinetic energy is conserved in a closed system
The angular momentum, which turns into energy

items.q: If the student could pull in until the system’s rotational inertia were one third of 3.0 kg·m², her angular velocity would be
options: 3 times as large, 6.0 rad/s
9 times as large, 18 rad/s
√3 times as large, about 3.5 rad/s
the same, 2.0 rad/s

items.q: What is the clay’s angular momentum about the pivot just before it hits?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the clay’s linear momentum. Multiply by the perpendicular distance from the pivot, 0.80 m.

items.q: What is the angular velocity of the rod and clay just after the collision?

mistakes.why: Value: that leaves out the clay’s own rotational inertia after it sticks, mr² = 0.032 kg·m².
Value: that uses linear momentum conservation. The pivot exerts an outside force during the collision, so use angular momentum about the pivot.

items.q: For the clay-rod system during the collision, which quantity stays the same?
options: Angular momentum about the pivot
Linear momentum of the clay and rod
Kinetic energy of the clay and rod
Each of momentum, angular momentum and energy

items.q: What fraction of the clay’s kinetic energy is left just after the collision?
options: About 11%
Nearly 100%
About 4%
About 50%

items.q: The angular momentum of a system stays constant when
options: the net external torque on it is zero
the net external force on the system is zero
no forces act inside the system
the system’s kinetic energy is constant

items.q: A diver leaves the board turning slowly, then tucks into a ball. Ignoring air, why does she turn faster in the tuck?
options: Her I falls while her angular momentum stays the same
Tucking pushes against the air and creates a torque
Gravity exerts a larger torque when she is tucked
Her kinetic energy is conserved, so she speeds up

items.q: A disk (I = 0.040 kg·m²) spins at 10 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A second disk (I = 0.020 kg·m²), not spinning, is dropped onto it on the same axle, and they turn together. What is their common angular velocity?

mistakes.why: Value: that keeps kinetic energy constant. The disks rub as they match speeds; use L = Iω.
Value: the inertias are swapped in the ratio.

items.q: A child runs tangent to the rim of a stationary merry-go-round and jumps on. For which system is angular momentum about the axle constant during the jump-on?
options: The child and the merry-go-round together
The child alone
The merry-go-round alone
Neither one, since the child pushes on the merry-go-round

items.q: A spinning ice skater on frictionless ice pulls her arms in. Predict how each quantity changes.
A star collapses to one hundredth of its radius, keeping its mass and shape. With no outside torque, its rotation rate becomes
options: 10,000 times as large
100 times as large
the same
one hundredth as large

items.q: In what order do the three objects reach the bottom?
options: Sphere, then disk, then hoop
Hoop, then disk, then sphere
A three-way tie: they have the same mass and radius
Disk, then sphere, then hoop

items.q: Use g = 9.8 m/s². What is the disk’s speed at the bottom?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the speed of an object that slides without spinning. A rolling disk also has rotational kinetic energy.
Value: that treats the disk like a hoop (I = MR²). For a disk, I = ½MR².

items.q: At the bottom, what fraction of the hoop’s kinetic energy is rotational?
options: One half
One third
Two sevenths
Zero

items.q: A second solid sphere with twice the mass and twice the radius rolls down the same ramp. Compared with the first sphere, its speed at the bottom is
options: the same
larger, because it is heavier
smaller, because it has more rotational inertia
smaller, because its radius is larger

items.q: A frictionless block, released from the top at the same moment, slides down beside them. Where does it finish?
options: First, ahead of all three
Last, because nothing makes it spin
Tied with the sphere
Between the disk and the hoop

items.q: From the data, when has the ball begun rolling without slipping?
options: By 1.2 s, when v_cm equals Rω
At 0.0 s, because the ball is moving
At 0.8 s, when ω reaches 35 rad/s
Not yet, because v_cm keeps falling

items.q: While the ball skids, which way does the lane’s friction force on the ball point, and what does it do?
options: Backward: it slows v_cm and speeds up the spin
Forward: it speeds up v_cm and the spin
Backward: it slows both v_cm and the spin
No friction acts, because the lane is level

items.q: What happens to the ball’s total kinetic energy during the skid (0 to 1.2 s)?
options: It decreases: kinetic friction dissipates energy
It stays the same: the spin gains what v_cm loses
It increases, because the ball starts to spin
It decreases to zero, because the ball stops skidding

items.q: After 1.2 s the ball rolls without slipping on the level lane. Ignoring air and the small losses in the lane, why do v_cm and ω stay constant?
options: Its contact point does not slide, so no friction acts
Static friction keeps pushing the ball forward
Kinetic friction balances the ball’s weight
The ball’s spin pushes it along the lane

items.q: For a ball of radius R rolling without slipping, the speed of its center is
options: v_cm = Rω
v_cm = ω/R
v_cm = 2Rω
v_cm = 0

items.q: A 0.60 kg solid ball (I = ⅖MR², given) rolls without slipping at 2.0 m/s. What is its total kinetic energy?

mistakes.why: Value: that is only the translational part. Add ½Iω² with ω = v/R.
Value: that adds a rotational part equal to the translational one, as for a hoop. For a solid ball it is ⅖ of it.

items.q: A wheel rolls without slipping down a ramp. The static friction force from the ramp
options: spins it up but does no work on it
dissipates energy, so less arrives at the bottom
points down the ramp and speeds up the center
is zero, because the wheel is not slipping

items.q: A hollow ball and a solid ball of the same mass and radius roll without slipping at the same speed. Predict how each quantity compares for the hollow ball.
A hoop rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp 1.2 m high. Use g = 9.8 m/s². What is its speed at the bottom?

mistakes.why: Value: that ignores the hoop’s spin. Half its kinetic energy is rotational.
Value: that is v². Take the square root: v = √(gh).

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.30 m rolls without slipping through 5.0 revolutions. How far does its center move?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 5.0 as the angle in radians. 5.0 revolutions = 10π rad.

items.q: What is the satellite’s speed at B?

mistakes.why: Value: the ratio is upside down. The satellite is slower where it is farther away: r_A v_A = r_B v_B.
Value: that scales v_A by √(r_A/r_B), the rule for circular orbits (v ∝ 1/√r). On an ellipse, use angular momentum: at A and B the velocity is perpendicular to r.

items.q: Why is the satellite’s angular momentum about Earth’s center the same at A and at B?
options: Earth’s pull on it points at Earth’s center: no torque
The satellite moves at a constant speed around it
Gravity does no work on a satellite
The satellite’s distance from Earth is constant

items.q: Which quantities for the satellite-Earth system are the same at A and at B?
options: Total mechanical energy and angular momentum
Kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy
Speed and distance from Earth
Kinetic energy and angular momentum

items.q: Taking U = 0 at infinite separation, how does the gravitational potential energy at A compare with that at B?
options: It is twice as negative at A
It is half as negative at A
It is four times as negative at A
It is the same at A and B

items.q: What is the satellite’s orbital speed?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the escape speed at this distance, √(2GM/r). A circular orbit needs √(GM/r).
Value: that is v². Take the square root.

items.q: What is the total mechanical energy of the satellite-planet system, with U = 0 at infinite separation?

mistakes.why: Value: the sign is wrong. A bound orbit has negative total energy: E = K + U with U = −2K.
Value: that is the gravitational potential energy alone. Add K = ½mv².

items.q: For this circular orbit, which relation holds?
options: E = −K and U = −2K
E = K and U = 0
E = 0, because the satellite stays in orbit
E = U, because the speed is constant

items.q: What speed would the satellite need, at this distance, to escape the planet completely?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the circular orbital speed. To escape, the total energy must reach zero: ½mv² = GMm/r.
Value: that doubles the orbital speed. Escape speed is √2 times it.

items.q: With U_G = 0 at infinite separation, a satellite in a bound orbit has total mechanical energy that is
options: negative
positive
zero
equal to its kinetic energy

items.q: A satellite moves from a circular orbit of radius r to one of radius 2r around the same planet. Its kinetic energy becomes
options: half as large
twice as large
one quarter as large
the same

items.q: A satellite in a circular orbit fires a short rocket burst that raises it to a larger circular orbit (after a second burst). Its total mechanical energy
options: increases, toward zero
decreases, because it moves more slowly
stays the same, because gravity is conservative
becomes positive

items.q: Earth has mass 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 6.4 × 10⁶ m. Ignoring air, what is the escape speed from its surface?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the speed of a low circular orbit. Escape needs E = 0: v = √(2GM/R).
Value: that is v². Take the square root.

items.q: A comet on a long elliptical orbit moves from its farthest point toward its closest point to the Sun. Predict how each quantity for the comet-Sun system changes.

variables.name: Gravitational potential energy of the comet-Sun system (zero at infinite separation)

items.q: Satellite X is in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet and moves at speed v. Satellite Y orbits the same planet in a circular orbit of radius 4r. Y’s speed is
options: 2v
v

items.q: Why does a satellite in a circular orbit keep the same speed all the way around?
options: Gravity is perpendicular to its velocity
There is no force on it in space
Its angular momentum is zero
A centrifugal force balances the pull
